Food, bonds, and stories

A book about the meals, relatives, and summers that raised me. I wrote it, illustrated it, and designed every page.

Syeda Abeeha ZahraFood illustrator, layout designer, and food photographer

Every story sits behind a sheet of printed butter paper.

Between each illustration and its story, a translucent leaf-bordered page turns the book into a family album, or a tray lined with baking parchment. You see the picture before you read it, like a memory not quite in focus.

The Mango Crate

Every summer, the crates arrive. Sent by relatives from another city, brought home from the market, or passed between neighbors like edible love letters. Mangoes, sun-warmed, golden, and a little bruised from the journey, mark the season better than calendars ever could. No spoons, no ceremony.
